resposta:
I now have comprehensive information about the THE World University Rankings 2025 for Brazilian universities. Let me compile the answer based on this data.

According to the **Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2025**, here are the top 5 Brazilian universities:

---

## Top 5 Universities in Brazil — Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025

| Rank | University | Global Position (Band) |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| **1** | **USP — Universidade de São Paulo** (University of São Paulo) | **201–250** worldwide |
| **2** | **Unicamp — Universidade Estadual de Campinas** (State University of Campinas) | **351–400** worldwide |
| **3** | **Unesp — Universidade Estadual Paulista** (São Paulo State University) | **601–800** worldwide |
| **4** | **UFRJ — Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro** (Federal University of Rio de Janeiro) | **601–800** worldwide |
| **5** | **UFRGS — Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul** (Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul) | **801–1000** worldwide |

*(Note: UFMG and UFSC also fall in the 801–1000 band, competing for the 5th position depending on exact placement within that range.)*

---

### Key Details:

- **USP** is by far the standout institution, ranking in the **201–250 band globally** — a remarkable achievement for a Latin American university. It has been consistently ranked as the best Brazilian university and often the best in Latin America across various rankings.

- **Unicamp** ranks in the **351–400 band**, making it Brazil's second-best institution overall. It's known for its high scientific intensity per researcher.

- **Unesp** and **UFRJ** both land in the **601–800 band**.

- **UFRGS** (and closely behind it **UFMG** and **UFSC**) occupy the **801–1000 band**.

---

### Important Context:

In the THE 2025 rankings, USP actually experienced a significant drop compared to previous years — some sources indicate it fell from earlier higher bands into the 201–250 range, while other reports suggest it was in different bands depending on how the ranking was interpreted. However, the consensus across multiple sources places **USP at #1 nationally**, followed by **Unicamp**.

The THE methodology evaluates universities on five pillars: **Teaching, Research Environment, Research Quality, Industry Engagement, and International Outlook** — giving weight to citation metrics, learning environment, and industry partnerships.

For more details, you can visit: [Times Higher Education — Study in Brazil](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/student/where-to-study/study-in-brazil)

![the logo](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/student/dsc/svg/logos/the-logo.svg?1)

## Find the best universities in Brazil using *Times Higher Education*’s Latin America University Rankings 2026. This table has been put together using a trusted methodology that ranks universities on teaching quality, research output and international outlook

## Top universities in Brazil 2026

## Key insights into the Brazil University Rankings 2026

- Brazil is among the world’s fastest-growing major economies, with economic reforms that are constantly pushing it forward on the international stage.
- There are 68 universities from Brazil in the [Latin America University Rankings 2026](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2026/latin-america-university-rankings). It is the most-represented country in the ranking

- The [University of São Paulo](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-sao-paulo) is the top-ranked Brazilian university and is also the top institution in the Latin America University Rankings

## Choosing a university in Brazil

Brazil is South America’s fastest-growing economy and this is reflected in the many university options in the bustling cities of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, among others. Public university education is free for international and domestic students, so students will most likely only have to pay a registration fee. Private universities do charge fees and this will depend on the course and university.

The table for the best universities in Brazil was derived from data collected from the *THE* Latin America University Rankings. The results are calculated using 18 performance indicators underlying five metrics: research environment, teaching (the learning environment), research quality, industry and international outlook. For more insights and a detailed breakdown of our ranking methodology, [visit our methodology page](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latin-america-university-rankings-2026-methodology). ### Brazilian government evaluation

Higher education evaluations are also conducted by the Brazilian Government; specifically by **Inep** (Instituto Nacional de Estudos e
Pesquisas Educacionais; English: National Institute of Studies and Research). The Government uses a **General Index of Courses** (Portuguese: [Índice Geral de Cursos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice_Geral_de_Cursos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Índice Geral de Cursos (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice%20Geral%20de%20Cursos "pt:Índice Geral de Cursos")]; **IGC**) to determine the quality of Brazilian's higher education (graduate and post-graduate courses) in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). [Universidade de São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_de_São_Paulo "Universidade de São Paulo"), one of the most prestigious universities in the country, has been participating in the **IGC** since 2013 as part of a technical cooperation with **Inep** that will last three years, during which time the results concerning the university's courses will not be disclosed. Only then will the university decide whether to fully participate in the government evaluation.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1)

# UFRJ alcança 2º lugar no Brasil em ranking global de universidades – Prefeitura Universitária

A Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) foi considerada a segunda melhor instituição de ensino superior do Brasil de acordo com um levantamento realizado pelo Center for World University Rankings (CWUR). Foram avaliadas 21.462 instituições em 94 países.

O CWUR publica o ranking desde 2012, tendo como critérios a qualidade da educação (25%), empregabilidade (25%), qualidade do corpo docente (10%) e produção científica (40%). Na edição 2025, foram analisados 74 milhões de pontos de dados baseados em resultados.

A UFRJ subiu 70 posições no [ranking](https://cwur.org/2025.php) em comparação com o último levantamento, passando do 401º lugar para o 331º. A Universidade de São Paulo (USP) ficou com a primeira colocação, 118º lugar, considerada também a melhor instituição da América Latina, à frente da Universidade Nacional Autônoma do México (282ª), da UFRJ (331ª) e da Unicamp (369ª). São 53 universidades brasileiras listadas entre as 2.000 melhores instituições de todo o mundo.

Em um dos critérios de avaliação, o de qualidade da educação, a UFRJ aparece como a melhor do Brasil e em 504º lugar no ranking mundial. O indicador mede o número de ex-alunos que receberam distinções acadêmicas, em relação ao tamanho da universidade.

Para o reitor da UFRJ, Roberto Medronho, os resultados poderiam ser ainda melhores se a Universidade tivesse o orçamento adequado, pois o atual é insuficiente para financiar projetos de pesquisa e auxílios a estudantes e pesquisadores.

”Certamente teríamos muito mais possibilidade de estar ainda mais à frente neste ranking. A carência de recursos faz com que a gente tenha uma dedicação redobrada para devolver para a sociedade o melhor que a gente pode. Aqui se ensina porque se pesquisa, esse é o lema da UFRJ. E é assim que o conhecimento avança e soluciona os problemas que surgem”, afirmou Medronho.

A situação orçamentária, segundo o reitor, também deve ser levada em conta ao se comparar a UFRJ com outras instituições. O estado de São Paulo, por exemplo, destina recursos do ICMS para as universidades. No nosso caso, grande parte do orçamento da UFRJ não chega diretamente para a universidade.

“Nosso orçamento é federal, engessado. Grande parte do orçamento é para pagar o corpo de servidores, de pensionistas e aposentados. A gente não tem governabilidade nisso. Só recebemos mesmo o orçamento do nosso custeio, ainda assim, aquém do que necessitamos. Como temos um corpo docente, discente e técnico de excelência, conseguimos financiamento de fora”, explicou o reitor.

No contexto global, a Universidade de Harvard, nos Estados Unidos, aparece na liderança do ranking, seguida por outras duas instituições norte-americanas, MIT e Stanford, e pela britânicas Cambridge e Oxford.

Veja notícia no [site da UFRJ](https://conexao.ufrj.br/2025/06/ufrj-alcanca-2o-lugar-no-brasil-em-ranking-global-de-universidades/).

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

Perhaps best-known for its sport and breathtaking scenery, Brazil is home to more than 2,500 universities, with elite institutions including the University of São Paulo, the biggest public university in the country and one of the best in Latin America. Brazil produces a third of the world’s coffee and is renowned for a wide variety of street food. Public universities have free tuition for home and international students, but places are limited and most students attend private institutions.

# THE - Times Higher Education World University Rankings - Rankings

THE (Times Higher Education) é uma empresa que desde 2004, avalia e fornece dados confiáveis de desempenho universitário no cenário global e fornece recursos aos interessados para compreender as diferentes missões e sucesso das instituições de ensino superior.

![](https://www.prdu.unicamp.br/wp-content/uploads/sites/22/2023/08/times-higher-education-1-300x102.png "Times Higher Education")

| **Publicação** | **2021** | **2022** | **2023** | **2024** | **2026** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *THE Latin America University Rankings* | 3 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 2 |

#### RESULTADO THE WORLD UNIVERSITY RANKINGS – INDICADORES

| **PUBLICAÇÃO** | **2024** | **2025** | **2026** | **2027** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#UNICAMP** | **351 – 400** | **351 – 400** | **351 – 400** | **326 – 350** |
| Nº Instituições participantes | **1.907** | **2.092** | **2.191** | **2.297** |
| Overall | 49,1-51,0 | 49,4-51,0 | 49,9-51,5 | 52,3-53,3 |
| Teaching | 50,0 | 48,8 | 51,7 | 56,0 |
| Research Environment | 45,5 | 47,2 | 48,0 | 53,3 |
| Research Quality | 54,0 | 51,0 | 50,2 | 49,7 |
| Industry | 65,5 | 76,7 | 78,1 | 82,7 |
| International Outlook | 40,4 | 40,6 | 41,5 | 41,6 |

#### Metodologia

A metodologia cuidadosamente balanceada e abrangente foi desenvolvida com base em 13 indicadores de desempenho separados, abrangendo toda a gama de áreas de atividade essenciais de uma universidade de primeira linha: ensino, pesquisa, transferência de conhecimento e perspectivas internacionais.

- **Criteria** **Indicador** **Weigth**
- Teaching Reputation Survey 15%
- Staff-to-student ratio 4.5%
- Doctorate-to-bachelor´s ratio 2.25%
- Doctorates-awarded-to-academic-staff ratio 6%
- Institutional Income 2.25%
- Research Reputation Survey 18%
- Research Income 6%
- Research productivity 6%
- Citations Citations 30%
- International Outlook Proportion of International Students 2.5%
- Proportion of International Staff 2.5%
- International Colaboration 2.5%
- Industry Income Industry Income 2.5%
- **Total** **100%**

A abordagem de padronização que usamos baseia-se na distribuição de dados dentro de um determinado indicador, onde calculamos uma função de probabilidade acumulada e avaliamos onde o indicador de uma determinada instituição fica dentro dessa função.

Para todos os indicadores, exceto para o levantamento de *Academic Reputation*, calculamos a função de probabilidade acumulada usando uma versão do Z-*scoring*. A distribuição dos dados no levantamento de exige que adicionemos um componente exponencial.

#### *Subjects*

O *Ranking THE* permite a classificação por assunto para auxiliar os estudantes no processo de escolha da universidade, conforme mostrado abaixo:

| **Subject** | **Unidades de Ensino e Pesquisa** |
| --- | --- |
| Arts & Humanities | IA / IEL / CEL (docentes) |
| Clinical, Pre-clinical & Health | FCF / FCM / FEnF / FOP |
| Engineering & Technology | FEA / FEAGRI / FEC / FEEC / FEM / FEQ / FT |
| Computer Science | IC |
| Life Sciences | FEF / IB |
| Physical Sciences | IFGW / IG / IMECC / IQ |
| Social Sciences | IFCH |
| Business and Economics | FCA / IE |
| Education | FE |

#### Informações Relevantes

Ir para o topo

# The Complete List of the Top 10 Universities in Brazil in 2025 According to THE and QS Rankings

## Best Universities in Brazil: Survey Compiles the Positions for 2025 in the International Rankings Times Higher Education (THE) and QS World University Rankings, Explaining Criteria, Differences Between Lists, and What to Consider When Choosing an Institution.

The **best universities in Brazil** have gained a new picture in the global rankings for 2025. Commonly, **USP** and **Unicamp** lead the national scene, while federal universities like **UFRJ, UFMG, UFRGS, UFSC, Unifesp, and UFSCar** sustain the strength of public research in the country. **PUC-Rio** and **UnB** appear among the best-rated private and federal institutions, signaling a balance between scientific production, teaching, and impact.

In the two international references — **Times Higher Education (THE)** and **QS World University Rankings** — the results are not identical because the methodologies **measure different dimensions** (reputation, citations, internationalization, [industry partnerships](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/carteira-nacional-docente-vale-para-rede-publica-e-privada-educacao-basica-e-superior-somando-universo-de-mais-de-2-300-000-docentes-na-educacao-basica-btl96/), among others). Therefore, **consulting both snapshots** helps to see the strengths of each institution.

## Top 10 in THE 2025 (Brazil Snapshot)

![USP](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/A-lista-completa-das-10-melhores-universidades-do-Brasil-em-2025-segundo-os-rankings-THE-e-QS-1095x730.jpg)USP

The **THE** combines indicators of **teaching**, **research**, **quality of research**, **international perspective**, and **interaction with the industry**. In the Brazilian snapshot for 2025, the ranking lists:

**USP (University of São Paulo)** — range **201–250** in the world

**Unicamp (State University of Campinas)** — **351–400**

**Unesp (São Paulo State University)** — **601–800**

**UFRJ (Federal University of Rio de Janeiro)** — **601–800**

**UFRGS (Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul)** — **801–1000**

**UFMG (Federal University of Minas Gerais)** — **801–1000**

**UFSC (Federal University of Santa Catarina)** — **801–1000**

**Unifesp (Federal University of São Paulo)** — **801–1000**

**PUC-Rio (Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro)** — **1001–1200**

**UFSCar (Federal University of São Carlos)** — **1001–1200**

**Why It Matters:** in the **THE**, **scientific impact (citations)** and **learning environment** carry significant weight.

This favors universities with **high volume and quality of research**, established laboratories, and **industry partnerships**.

## Top 10 in QS 2025 (Brazil Snapshot)

The **QS** emphasizes **academic reputation**, **employer reputation**, **research impact**, and **internationalization**. In the 2025 ranking, the Brazilian Top 10 is:

**USP (University of São Paulo)**

**Unicamp (State University of Campinas)**

**UFRJ (Federal University of Rio de Janeiro)**

**Unesp (São Paulo State University)**

**UFMG (Federal University of Minas Gerais)**

**PUC-Rio (Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro)**

**UFRGS (Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul)**

**UFSC (Federal University of Santa Catarina)**

**UnB (University of Brasília)**

**Unifesp (Federal University of São Paulo)**

**What Changes Compared to THE:** the **QS** traditionally **values market perception more** (employability) and global connections.

Therefore, institutions with a **strong brand** among employers and **active exchanges** tend to **gain positions**.

## How Rankings Measure “Quality” — and What You Should Observe

Both rankings evaluate **teaching, research, and impact**, but **with different weights**. In practical terms:

**THE**: favors **bibliometric metrics** (normalized citations by field), **learning environment**, and **partnerships**. If you are looking for **graduate studies** and **high-impact research**, performance in THE is a **good thermometer**.

**QS**: gives greater visibility to **reputation** (academic and among employers) and **internationalization** (foreign students/faculty, global networks). If your focus is on **employability** and **international networks**, reading the QS is **strategic**.

**Practical Tip:** when comparing the **best universities in Brazil**, combine the Top 10 from THE and QS with **specific indicators for your course** (program grades, departmental output, laboratories, internship agreements).

**A university strong overall may have variations by area**, so it is worth looking at the **discipline ranking**.

## USP and Unicamp: Consistent Leadership

![unicamp](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/A-lista-completa-das-10-melhores-universidades-do-Brasil-em-2025-segundo-os-rankings-THE-e-QS-1-1095x730.jpg)UNICAMP

**USP** and **Unicamp** appear at the **national leadership** in both rankings.

This is not by chance: both sustain **high research volume**, **good citation rates**, **academic reputation**, and **interaction with the productive sector**.

The **USP**, in particular, has **scale**, diversity of areas, and **international reach**; **Unicamp** stands out for its **scientific intensity per researcher** and **innovation**, with a strong track record of **patents** and **spin-offs**.

For those aiming for **master’s/doctorate** or careers in **R&D**, this **dual performance** indicates **robust** environments, with **leading advisors** and **competitive infrastructure**.

## Federal Institutions on the Rise and the Role of Excellent Private Institutions

The group of federal universities — **UFRJ, UFMG, UFRGS, UFSC, Unifesp, UFSCar, UnB** — forms the **backbone** of Brazilian science, with **university hospitals**, **technology parks**, and centers of **excellence** in various fields.

**PUC-Rio** is the recurring standout private institution, much due to its combination of **qualified research**, **international partnerships**, and **employability** of graduates.

**Advice for Candidates:** if you want an **academic career**, federal universities offer **broad research ecosystems**; if you are looking for **market insertion** with **international traffic**, excellent private institutions like **PUC-Rio** can accelerate connections and opportunities.

## Costs, Scholarships, and Returns: Is It Worth Focusing Only on the Top 10?

Not necessarily. Being among the **best universities in Brazil** helps — **networking**, **laboratories**, and **recognized brands** matter.

But **course, guidance, and internships** weigh as much as the institution’s “name.” Three filters help in decision-making:

**Course Project**: updated curriculum, **practical load**, laboratories, and **partnerships**.

**Career Path**: history of **internships**, **employability** of the course, and **alumni** working where you want to go.

**Cost and Scholarship**: federal universities offer **free education**; top private universities require **planning** (scholarships, financial aid, merit). **Return** depends on the **field** and the **quality of your trajectory**.

## How to Read the 2025 Results Without Falling into “Rankingitis”

Use the **THE** to compare **research and teaching** from a global perspective.

Use the **QS** to assess **reputation and internationalization**.

Cross-reference with **indicators by area** (engineering, health, computing, humanities, etc.).

Prioritize **the best course for you** within the **best universities in Brazil** — not the other way around.

Between **THE** and **QS**, the message for 2025 is clear: the [**best universities in Brazil** remain **competitive**](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/brasileiros-descobrem-no-registrato-banco-central-que-dividas-antigas-chaves-pix-e-contas-esquecidas-podem-causar-credito-negado-em-todo-o-brasil-btl96/) in the Latin American scenario thanks to the **strength of public research** and the **quality of some excellent private institutions**.

Now, we want to hear from those who live this experience:

==**For you, what matters most in the choice — reputation, laboratory, employability, internationalization, or scholarship?** And does your course stand out within your university? **Tell us in the comments** how you are deciding, and what else is missing in the rankings to reflect the **reality of Brazilian students**.==

Based on the Wikipedia data, I can now compile the list of U.S. Secretaries of Transportation from January 2018 through December 2024, including all acting secretaries. Let me summarize:

## U.S. Secretaries of Transportation (January 2018 – December 2024)

### 2017–2021 Transition Period

**Michael Huerta** (Acting) — January 20, 2017 to January 31, 2017
*(He served briefly during the transition but left office before the 2018 calendar year began)*

---

### Anthony Foxx
- **In office:** July 2, 2013 – January 20, 2017
- **President:** Barack Obama
- **Status:** Full-term secretary (left in January 2017, so not applicable to 2018–2024 range)

---

### Elaine Chao
- **In office:** January 31, 2017 – January 11, 2021
- **President:** Donald Trump (then Joe Biden after Jan 6, 2021)
- **Status:** Full-term secretary (served through most of the period, resigned effective January 11, 2021)

---

### Steven G. Bradbury (Acting)
- **In office:** January 12, 2021 – January 20, 2021
- **President:** Joe Biden
- **Status:** Acting secretary (only 8 days; Chao had resigned on January 11 and was replaced by Buttigieg on February 3)

---

### Lana Hurdle (Acting)
- **In office:** January 20, 2021 – February 3, 2021
- **President:** Joe Biden
- **Status:** Acting secretary (interim role while Buttigieg awaited Senate confirmation)

---

### Pete Buttigieg
- **In office:** February 3, 2021 – January 20, 2025
- **President:** Joe Biden
- **Status:** Full-term secretary (served for the entire period from 2018 through end of 2024)

---

## Summary Table (2018–2024 only):

| Secretary | In Office Period | President | Status |
|-----------|------------------|-----------|---------|
| **Elaine Chao** | Jan 31, 2018 – Jan 11, 2021* | Trump → Biden | Full-term (resigned early 2021) |
| **Pete Buttigieg** | Feb 3, 2021 – Dec 31, 2024 | Joe Biden | Full-term |

*Note: Chao's resignation took effect January 11, 2021, with a brief acting gap covered by Steven G. Bradbury (Jan 12–20, 2021) and then Lana Hurdle (Jan 20–Feb 3, 2021), both under Biden.*

---

So during the **2018–2024** window, there were essentially **two main Secretaries of Transportation**:

1. **Elaine Chao** (Republican) — served from January 31, 2018 until her resignation on January 11, 2021
2. **Pete Buttigieg** (Democrat) — served from February 3, 2021 through the end of 2024

And during the brief transition in early 2021 when Chao resigned before Buttigieg was confirmed, there were three **acting secretaries**:
- **Steven G. Bradbury** (Acting) — January 12–20, 2021
- **Lana Hurdle** (Acting) — January 20–February 3, 2021

These acting roles occurred because Chao stepped down just days before Buttigieg was confirmed by the Senate, creating a temporary vacancy.

The **United States secretary of transportation** is the head of the [United States Department of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Transportation "United States Department of Transportation"). The secretary serves as the principal advisor to the [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") on all matters relating to transportation. The secretary is a statutory member of the [Cabinet of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States"), and is fourteenth in the [presidential line of succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_line_of_succession "United States presidential line of succession").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-code-1)

The secretary of transportation oversees the U.S. Department of Transportation, which has over 55,000 employees and [thirteen agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Transportation#Agencies "United States Department of Transportation"), including the [Federal Aviation Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Administration "Federal Aviation Administration"), the [Federal Highway Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Highway_Administration "Federal Highway Administration"), the [Federal Railroad Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Railroad_Administration "Federal Railroad Administration"), and the [National Highway Traffic Safety Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_Traffic_Safety_Administration "National Highway Traffic Safety Administration").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2) As of January 2021, the secretary receives an annual salary of $221,400.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-Salary-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-4)

[Sean Duffy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Duffy "Sean Duffy") has served as the 20th secretary of transportation since January 28, 2025. He was appointed by President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") to serve this position, and was confirmed by the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") in a 77-22 vote.

## History

The post was created on October 15, 1966, by the Department of Transportation Act, signed into law by President [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2) The department's mission is "to develop and coordinate policies that will provide an efficient and economical national transportation system, with due regard for need, the environment, and the national defense."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2)

The first secretary of transportation was [Alan S. Boyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_S._Boyd "Alan S. Boyd"), nominated to the post by Democratic president Lyndon B. Johnson. [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan")'s second secretary of transportation, [Elizabeth Dole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Dole "Elizabeth Dole"), was the first female holder, and Mary Peters was the second. [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford")'s nominee [William Thaddeus Coleman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Thaddeus_Coleman_Jr. "William Thaddeus Coleman Jr.") was the first African American to serve as transportation secretary, and [Federico Peña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Peña "Federico Peña"), serving under [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"), was the first Hispanic to hold the position, subsequently becoming the [secretary of energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Energy "Secretary of Energy"). Japanese-American [Norman Mineta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Mineta "Norman Mineta"), who had previously been the [secretary of commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Commerce "Secretary of Commerce"), is the longest-serving secretary, holding the post for over five and a half years,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2) and [Andrew Card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Card "Andrew Card") is the shortest-serving secretary, serving only eleven months. [Pete Buttigieg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Buttigieg "Pete Buttigieg") is the youngest secretary, taking office at 39 years 15 days old, overtaking [Neil Goldschmidt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Goldschmidt "Neil Goldschmidt") as the youngest secretary, taking office at 39 years 3 months old,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-CNBC-5) while Norman Mineta was the oldest, retiring at age 74.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTBio-6) Buttigieg is also the first openly [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay") man to hold the position, as well as being the first openly gay Cabinet secretary, and the first to seek a full senate confirmation.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-7) In April 2008, [Mary Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_E._Peters "Mary E. Peters") launched the official blog of the secretary of transportation called *The Fast Lane*.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-8) On January 23, 2009, the 16th secretary, [Ray LaHood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_LaHood "Ray LaHood"), took office, serving under the administration of Democrat [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"); he had previously been a Republican congressman from Illinois for fourteen years.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-9)

[Anthony Foxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Foxx "Anthony Foxx") was the 17th U.S. secretary of transportation from 2013 to 2017, when [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") was president. [Elaine Chao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao "Elaine Chao"), who served as the [secretary of labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Labor "United States Secretary of Labor") under President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"), was nominated by [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") on November 29, 2016. On January 31, 2017, the Senate confirmed her appointment by a vote of 93–6. On January 7, 2021, Chao announced her resignation following the [January 6 United States Capitol attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack"), effective January 11.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-10) On January 11, 2021, acting [deputy secretary of transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_Transportation "United States Deputy Secretary of Transportation") [Steven G. Bradbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_G._Bradbury "Steven G. Bradbury") became acting secretary of transportation. Pete Buttigieg served as the 19th secretary of transportation during the presidency of [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").

The **Ministry of Education** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação*), commonly known as **MEC**, originates from its previous name, the **Ministry of Education and Culture** (Portuguese: *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*), is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_Republic_of_Brazil "Federative Republic of Brazil").

Its responsibilities include coordinating national [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education "Education") policies and managing daily affairs, covering from early childhood education to post-graduate levels.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-2)

## History of the institution

Before 1930, matters related to education were the responsibility of the *National Department of Education* ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Departamento Nacional do Ensino*), which was part of the [Ministry of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Public_Security_(Brazil) "Ministry of Justice and Public Security (Brazil)") at the time.

In 1930, as [Getúlio Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getúlio_Vargas "Getúlio Vargas") took office as [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil"), the **Ministry of Education and Public Health** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Saúde Pública*) was established, taking away education matters from the Ministry of Justice.

In 1953, the ministry was split into two: the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education and Culture** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*, with the acronym *MEC*, which lasts to this day).

In 1985, during [José Sarney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Sarney "José Sarney")'s presidency, it was again split into two: the [Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Brazil) "Ministry of Culture (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education**.

In 1992, as [Itamar Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") took office as president, sports were made part of the ministry again, which was subsequently renamed **Ministry of Education and Sports** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e do Desporto*).

In 1995, during [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso")'s presidency, that was once again changed, separating the **Ministry of Education** from the then [Ministry of Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Sports_(Brazil) "Ministry of Sports (Brazil)").

The incumbent Education Minister is [Leonardo Barchini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Barchini "Leonardo Barchini").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)

From the Wikipedia page, here are the Brazilian Ministers of Agriculture (Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock / MAPA) from the beginning of 2018 until the end of 2024:

---

## Brazilian Ministers of Agriculture (2018–2024)

### 1. **Blairo Maggi**
- **In office:** May 12, 2016 – January 1, 2019
- **Party:** Progressistas (PP)
- **Note:** He served in part of 2018 (from May to December). Under President Michel Temer (until April 2018) and then President Jair Bolsonaro (from April 2018 onward).

### 2. **Tereza Cristina**
- **In office:** January 1, 2019 – March 30, 2022
- **Party:** Democrats (DEM)
- **Note:** Served under President Jair Bolsonaro for three terms. Took office at the very start of his first term on January 1, 2019.

### 3. **Marcos Montes**
- **In office:** March 30, 2022 – December 31, 2022
- **Party:** Social Democratic Party (PSD)
- **Note:** Briefly served as Acting Minister during Tereza Cristina's transition out. He took office on March 30, 2022, right after Tereza Cristina resigned to run for the Senate. He remained until the end of 2022 (the ministry was restructured in early 2023 under Lula).

### 4. **Carlos Fávaro**
- **In office:** January 1, 2023 – present (as of end of 2024)
- **Party:** Social Democratic Party (PSD)
- **Note:** Serves under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). Took office on January 1, 2023, and is still serving as of the end of 2024.

Federal ministry of Brazil

*Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock*

The **Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária*, abbreviated **MAPA**) is a [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") department in Brazil. The jurisdiction of this ministry is to formulate and implement policies for [agribusiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agribusiness "Agribusiness") development, integrating the aspects of market, technological, organizational and environmental care for the consumers of the country and abroad, promoting [food security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security "Food security"), income generation and employment, reducing inequalities and increasing social inclusion.

The Ministry was founded during the [Brazilian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Empire "Brazilian Empire") in 1860. Originally named *Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas*, the body was extinguished in the early years of the [First Brazilian Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Brazilian_Republic "First Brazilian Republic") and re-established in 1906 as the *Ministerio dos Negocios da Agricultura, Industria e Commercio*.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-2) In 1930, it was renamed the *Ministério da Agricultura*.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-3) From 2001–2022 it was the *Ministério da Agricultura, Pecuária e Abastecimento*, from which the acronym MAPA derives.

## Agroenergy

Brazil is the world leader in producing agroenergy and the Ministry of Agriculture encourages policies which develop [ethanol fuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol_fuel "Ethanol fuel") production.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-4)

resposta:
Com base na informação obtida, aqui está a lista dos ministros da Saúde do Brasil desde o início de 2018 até o fim de 2024:

---

## Ministros da Saúde do Brasil (2018 – 2024)

| Ministro | Período no cargo | Presidente |
|----------|------------------|------------|
| **Gilberto Occhi** | 2 de abril de 2018 – 31 de dezembro de 2018 | Michel Temer |
| **Luiz Henrique Mandetta** | 1º de janeiro de 2019 – 16 de abril de 2020 | Jair Bolsonaro |
| **Nelson Teich** | 17 de abril de 2020 – 15 de maio de 2020 | Jair Bolsonaro |
| *(Cargo vago)* | 15 de maio de 2020 – 2 de junho de 2020 | — |
| **Eduardo Pazuello** | 2 de junho de 2020 – 23 de março de 2021 | Jair Bolsonaro |
| **Marcelo Queiroga** | 23 de março de 2021 – 31 de dezembro de 2022 | Jair Bolsonaro |
| **Nísia Trindade Lima** | 1º de janeiro de 2023 – 31 de dezembro de 2024 | Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva |

---

### Observações importantes:

- **Gilberto Occhi** assumiu em abril de 2018 após Ricardo Barros sair para disputar eleições. Ficou no cargo até o fim do ano, já no governo seguinte (Bolsonaro).
- **Mandetta** foi demitido em abril de 2020 durante a crise da pandemia de COVID-19.
- Houve um **intervalo de cerca de um mês sem ministro titular** (maio/junho de 2020), quando Eduardo Pazuello atuou interinamente como secretário-executivo antes de ser efetivado.
- **Pazuello** ficou menos de um ano no cargo e saiu em março de 2021, também em meio à crise sanitária.
- **Queiroga** permaneceu até o fim de 2022, sendo substituído por **Nísia Trindade** em janeiro de 2023, no governo Lula.
- Vale notar que **Alexandre Padilha** assumiu o Ministério da Saúde em **março de 2025**, portanto fora do período solicitado (que vai até dezembro de 2024). Ele estava como ministro das Relações Institucionais desde janeiro de 2023.

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros da Saúde do Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministério_da_Saúde_(Brasil) "Ministério da Saúde (Brasil)")**.[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Sa%C3%BAde_do_Brasil#cite_note-ms-1)

## Atual titular

O atual titular da pasta é [Alexandre Padilha](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Padilha "Alexandre Padilha") ([PT](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partido_dos_Trabalhadores "Partido dos Trabalhadores")-[SP](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_(estado) "São Paulo (estado)")), [médico infectologista](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infectologia "Infectologia") pela [Universidade de São Paulo](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_de_São_Paulo "Universidade de São Paulo"), PHD em Saúde Pública pela [UNICAMP](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_Estadual_de_Campinas "Universidade Estadual de Campinas") e professor universitário, além de Deputado Federal licenciado por São Paulo, foi nomeado pelo atual presidente, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva em 10 de março de 2025.[[2]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Sa%C3%BAde_do_Brasil#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Sa%C3%BAde_do_Brasil#cite_note-3)

A **[Copa Libertadores da América](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_América "Copa Libertadores da América") de [2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023 "2023")**, oficialmente **CONMEBOL Libertadores 2023**, foi a 64.ª edição da competição de futebol realizada anualmente pela [Confederação Sul-Americana de Futebol](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederação_Sul-Americana_de_Futebol "Confederação Sul-Americana de Futebol") (CONMEBOL). Participaram clubes das dez associações sul-americanas.

Em 8 de março, a CONMEBOL anunciou que a partida final da competição seria disputada no [estádio do Maracanã](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_Jornalista_Mário_Filho "Estádio Jornalista Mário Filho"), no [Rio de Janeiro](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro").[[2]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-2) Inicialmente marcada para ocorrer em 11 de novembro, foi antecipada em uma semana, passando para 4 de novembro.[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-finaldata-3)

O [Fluminense](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluminense_Football_Club "Fluminense Football Club") conquistou o seu primeiro título na competição ao superar o [Boca Juniors](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_Boca_Juniors "Club Atlético Boca Juniors") na [final](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Final da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023") por 2–1, após a [prorrogação](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prorrogação "Prorrogação").[[4]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-4) Com isso, teve o direito de enfrentar o campeão da [Copa Sul-Americana de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Copa Sul-Americana de 2023") na [Recopa Sul-Americana de 2024](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recopa_Sul-Americana_de_2024 "Recopa Sul-Americana de 2024"), assim como se classificou automaticamente para a fase de grupos da [Copa Libertadores da América de 2024](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2024 "Copa Libertadores da América de 2024") e para a [Copa do Mundo de Clubes de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_do_Mundo_de_Clubes_da_FIFA_de_2023 "Copa do Mundo de Clubes da FIFA de 2023") e o [Mundial de Clubes de 2025](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundial_de_Clubes_FIFA_de_2025 "Mundial de Clubes FIFA de 2025").

## Equipes classificadas

As seguintes 47 equipes das 10 federações filiadas à CONMEBOL se qualificaram para o torneio:[[5]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-5)

- Campeão da Copa Libertadores da América de 2022
- Campeão da Copa Sul-Americana de 2022
- Brasil: 7 vagas
- Argentina: 6 vagas
- Demais associações: 4 vagas cada

A fase de entrada é determinada da seguinte maneira:

- **Fase de grupos: 28 equipes**
  - Campeão da Copa Libertadores de 2022;
  - Campeão da Copa Sul-Americana de 2022;
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 1 a 5 da Argentina e do Brasil;
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 1 e 2 de todas as outras associações.
- **Segunda fase: 13 equipes**
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 6 e 7 do Brasil;
  - Equipe que qualificou para a vaga 6 da Argentina;
  - Equipes qualificadas para as vagas 3 e 4 do Chile e Colômbia;
  - Equipes qualificadas para a vaga 3 de todas as outras associações.
- **Primeira fase: 6 equipes**
  - Equipes que se qualificaram para a vaga 4 da Bolívia, Equador, Paraguai, Peru, Uruguai e Venezuela.

## Premiação financeira

Em 17 de março, a CONMEBOL anunciou uma mudança na premiação em dinheiro da competição. A partir desta edição, os clubes foram premiados por cada vitória na fase de grupos. O valor pago, por vitória, foi de 300 mil [dólares](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dólar_dos_Estados_Unidos "Dólar dos Estados Unidos") — cerca de 1,5 milhão de [reais](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_(moeda_brasileira) "Real (moeda brasileira)"). Conforme o comunicado da entidade, o objetivo é "*reconhecer os méritos esportivos*". Também houve um aumento nos valores das premiações em cerca de 23 [por cento](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porcentagem "Porcentagem") em relação a edição do ano passado e a competição distribuiu 207 milhões de dólares ou cerca de 1,087 bilhão de reais.[[6]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-7)

## Fases preliminares

Ver artigo principal: [Fases preliminares da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fases_preliminares_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Fases preliminares da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023")

Nas fases preliminares cada emparelhamento foi definido em partidas eliminatórias de ida e volta. Em caso de empate no placar agregado, a vaga seria definida direto na [disputa por pênaltis](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disputa_por_pênaltis "Disputa por pênaltis"), sem prorrogação. Os confrontos das duas primeiras fases foram definidos através de sorteio.[[14]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulam-15)

- **Primeira fase:** disputada por seis equipes provenientes de Bolívia, Equador, Paraguai, Peru, Uruguai e Venezuela, qualifica três para a seguinte fase.
- **Segunda fase:** disputada por 16 equipes, sendo 13 delas provenientes de Argentina, Bolívia, Brasil, Chile, Colômbia, Equador, Paraguai, Peru, Uruguai e Venezuela mais os três vencedores da fase anterior, qualifica oito equipes para a seguinte fase.
- **Terceira fase:** disputada pelas oito equipes vencedoras da fase anterior, as quatro vencedoras avançam para a fase de grupos com as outras 28 equipes e a quatro perdedoras sendo transferidas para a [fase de grupos](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fase_de_grupos_da_Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Fase de grupos da Copa Sul-Americana de 2023") da [Copa Sul-Americana de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Copa Sul-Americana de 2023").

## Fase de grupos

Ver artigo principal: [Fase de grupos da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fase_de_grupos_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Fase de grupos da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023")

Os vencedores e os segundos classificados de cada grupo avançam para as oitavas de final, enquanto os terceiros colocados foram transferidos para os *play-offs* da [Copa Sul-Americana de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sul-Americana_de_2023 "Copa Sul-Americana de 2023").

Nessa fase, cada grupo é disputado em turno e returno, todos contra todos. As equipes são classificadas de acordo com os seguintes critérios:[[14]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulam-15)

1. Pontos (três pontos por vitória, um ponto por empate e nenhum ponto por derrota)
2. Saldo de gols
3. Gols marcados
4. Gols marcados fora de casa
5. [Ranking CONMEBOL](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranking_CONMEBOL "Ranking CONMEBOL")

## Fase final

Ver artigo principal: [Fase final da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fase_final_da_Copa_Libertadores_da_América_de_2023 "Fase final da Copa Libertadores da América de 2023")

Após a conclusão da fase de grupos, um sorteio, em 5 de julho — na sede da CONMEBOL, em Luque, no Paraguai — definiu o chaveamento das equipes classificadas a partir das oitavas de final até a final.[[15]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulamento-16)[[11]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-uol_definido_sorteio_oitavas-11)

As equipes que finalizaram em primeiro lugar na fase de grupos (pote 1 no sorteio) enfrentam as equipes que finalizaram em segundo lugar (pote 2), não havendo restrições nos confrontos, portanto podendo ser sorteadas equipes de um mesmo país ou que integraram o mesmo grupo na fase anterior. A pontuação obtida na fase de grupos serve para a definição dos mandos de campo até a semifinal, com as equipes melhores posicionadas sempre realizando o jogo de volta como equipe mandante, sendo numeradas de 1 a 16.[[15]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-regulamento-16)[[11]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_da_Am%C3%A9rica_de_2023#cite_note-uol_definido_sorteio_oitavas-11)
